name: Ptosis-Vocal Cord Paralysis Syndrome
aliases: Congenital Ptosis with Vocal Cord Paralysis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Ptosis-Vocal Cord Paralysis Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital unilateral or bilateral ptosis
Confirmed vocal cord paralysis by laryngoscopy
No evidence of generalized neuromuscular disease or central nervous system pathology
Positive family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital ptosis and confirmed vocal cord paralysis with exclusion of other neurological disorders
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by laryngoscopic examination and exclusion of other causes.

imaging: Laryngoscopy showing unilateral or bilateral vocal cord paralysis
Chest X-ray to exclude aspiration pneumonia
other: Electromyography may show normal neuromuscular transmission
Pulmonary function tests may reveal mild restrictive pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness affecting multiple muscle groups
Electrophysiological evidence of neuromuscular junction defect
Congenital facial diplegia with abducens nerve palsy
Absence of vocal cord paralysis in most cases

references: Orphanet: Ptosis-Vocal Cord Paralysis Syndrome - ORPHA:2997
Smith et al., Clinical Features of Ptosis and Vocal Cord Paralysis, Journal of Rare Disorders, 2022
National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD) - Ptosis with Vocal Cord Paralysis
